title: Correctness of the input-cell update
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state multi-tape Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $\ell$ be a list of circuit bit sources, let $T,t,p\in\mathbb N$, let $x$ be a binary string, and let $B$ be a list of binary blocks. Suppose every source $s$ in $\ell$ has the same value on $(x,B)$ as on $(x,[])$. Suppose also that every block of index $i'<t\bigl(k(2T+1)+|\ell|+3\bigr)+k(2T+1)+p$ equals the configuration encoding at index $i'$ generated from the list of source values on $(x,[])$, where $k$ is the number of work tapes of $M$. If $p<|\ell|+2$, then applying the input-cell update to the values of the padded input-cell source list for time $t$ and position $p$ gives exactly the input-cell encoding at that time and position for the binary input whose bits are the values of the sources in $\ell$ on $(x,[])$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite-state multi-tape Turing machine M over the binary alphabet
A list ℓ of circuit bit sources and a natural number T
A natural number t and a position p
A binary string x and a list B of binary blocks
Each source in ℓ has equal evaluation on (x,B) and (x,[])
Every block with index less than the input index has the specified configuration-encoding value
caveat: The claim uses the particular input-cell source, padding, update, and encoding constructions; their full constructions are not described in the supplied informal definitions.
